The draft reads the 12-mile week correctly as marathon recovery: 41 miles with the race inside it, legs back by Thursday. It turns down 40 miles and speedwork, says why, and gives a ladder back up (23, then 30, then 36–40). Next week is safe. Every run is easy and conversational. There are two full rest days, the only quick running is 4 x 20-second strides, and the long run is 7 miles. Going from 12 to 23 miles is a big jump on paper, but she was at about 40 before the race, so this still counts as easing back to consistency (check 7). It is not a sharp jump. She is fully rested and nothing hurts, so no other must-never check applies. Every day can be run as written.

What keeps it from a 5:
- It says the race was "14 days ago." Going by the weekly totals, the race looks more like a week back. The extra week happens to make the advice more cautious, which is the safer direction, but it is still a slip.
- The timeline contradicts itself. It says "about three more weeks before real intensity," then puts the first tempo work "in two weeks," which is the third step of its own ladder.
- The heart-rate caps (145 and 150) aren't based on anything she reported.
- It doesn't take up her switch to a 10K goal, beyond pushing the speedwork back.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 42, 46, 34, 41 mi
This week: 12 mi over 3 runs.
Body: "Legs came back by Thursday. Blister healed."
Feeling: "Itching to train again."
Asks: "I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Great recovery week and a strong signal that the legs are turning over again, but we are only two weeks out from a marathon, so…
Answers: (1) Not quite yet, and here is the honest version. You raced a marathon 14 days ago; the common rule of thumb is roughly one easy day per mile raced before full training resumes, so about three more weeks before real intensity. (2) What I would rather do: climb to about 23 mi next week, 30 mi the week after, then 36–40 mi with the first light faster work (strides and short tempo) in two weeks. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off keeps the recovery curve going; no cross-training needed.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, conversational, heart rate under 145. First run back into your normal…
Wed: easy, 5 mi, conversational, then 4 x 20 sec strides at the end on flat ground, full…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, very relaxed, heart rate under 145. Short shakeout between…
Fri: rest. Protects the Saturday–Sunday block.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, conversational. Primer for Sunday.
Sun: easy, 7 mi, conversational the whole way, heart rate under 150. Gentle step back…
